citations.field: PDF p.1282; printed p.1267; 六 entry
citations.text: The 六 entry identifies the graph as a pictograph resembling a simple shelter. It says Shang oracle-bone forms resemble a shelter set on the ground and later forms emphasize the shelter wall; Qin small-seal form curves the two upper strokes inward, and clerical transformation changes them into a dot and horizontal stroke. It proposes a grass hut as the original meaning and 六 as an early graph for 廬, later borrowed for the numeral because the sounds were close. It also connects 六 with the yin line in the Changes. I directly inspected the full page image, including the 六 heading, glyph sequence, source notes, and complete paragraph; this is one attributed proposal, not conclusive evidence of the graph’s origin.
